segments.approved_text: Bitcoin has now seen a 16 % decline from the overall high from $88 ,000, touching down towards about $73 ,400, $500, give or take.

It went from above $81 ,000 after the election to below $75 ,000 by the weekend. U .S. Bitcoin ETFs had about $1 .3 billion in net outflows just last week. And Bitcoin really hasn't participated in the Monday rally.

Of course, Bitcoin dropped pretty massively over the weekend alongside the tech sell -off that we saw, the Democrat blue wave, the Binance hack. But I don't check it on an hourly basis. It seemed to have bounced very nicely at a very key level around $74 ,000, around the 50 -weekly MA, which we've talked about many times.

Last night was Bitcoin's first weekly close below the 50 -week moving average since September. The 50 -week was around $75 ,500, and Bitcoin closed around $74 ,700, just 1 % below the line. But one percent is still a miss.
